whyMindsetDescFirst: Mindset was born in 2024 with the desire to make its contribution in an ecosystem where esport is taking more and more place; bring a vision that invites introspection and consider its place within this community.
whyMindsetDescSecond: Convinced that diversity is a strength and talent pool , Mindset is an inclusive esport event promoting versus fighting and each member of the fighting games community.
whyMindsetDescThird: We want to create an identity and an environment of trust where anyone who identifies with it can fully express themselves through a common passion.
whyMindsetDescFourth: Promote accessibility and inclusivity by creating a healthy environment governed by principles and values such as fair play, surpassing oneself, selfknowledge, self-esteem, resilience, adaptation...

rulesSF6Title: Rules of the Street Fighter 6 tournament
ruleGlobal: The tournaments are open to people who are eighteen (18) years older on the date of their tournament registration. Any minor must be accompanied by a parent to participate in the event.
rulesPreambule: The fighting game community belongs to everyone. As members of the FGC, we consider it our responsibility to represent, foster and enforce values which safeguard and empower its events, players, and fans. We believe all members of the fighting game community share this responsibility with us. As a result, we expect any group or individual who wishes to attend or be a part of Mindset in any capacity to behave according to our Mindset Values and abide by our Code of Conduct. Any group or individual who is unable or unwilling to do so will no longer be welcome at Mindset.
valueCommunity: Community - We consider ourselves lucky to be a member of the fighting game community, and believe we should work to be a force for good within it. We are dedicated to building up this community and its members, and expect the same of others. We will not tolerate any actions which undermine this community or threaten the health, safety, or welfare of any of its members.
ValueRespect: Respect - Everyone matters, everyone contributes, and everyone is welcome at Mindset. We will not tolerate violence, bullying, harassment, intimidation, racism, intolerance, discrimination, marginalization, or threats directed against anyone at any time.
ValueIntegrity: Integrity - We hold ourselves, our staff, our competitors, and our fans to the highest standard of integrity. Cheating, scamming, fraud, theft, impersonation, and other deceptive, dangerous or illegal activities will not be tolerated, and will be prosecuted when appropriate.
ValueGlobal: In order to keep Mindset and the FGC open and welcoming to everyone, it is important for all our users to respect the rights of others, as outlined above. Accordingly, when you attend or participate in any NSxC event in any capacity, you are agreeing to represent and uphold our values as well as to follow the rules set forth below.
Prohibition1: Do not bully, threaten, harm, troll, harass or stalk anyone, or encourage others to do so.
Prohibition2: Do not use or promote hate speech, slurs, or other abusive or offensive language.
Prohibition3: Do not cheat, or use or exploit any bugs, glitches, vulnerabilities or unintentional mechanics to get a competitive advantage for yourself or others.
Prohibition4: Do not engage in or encourage lewd, vulgar, or offensive behavior, or in any other behavior that may disrupt gameplay or our events, or others’ enjoyment of them.
Prohibition5: Do not disparage or discriminate against anyone based on their race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, nationality, religion, appearance, mental or physical ability, or other personal characteristics.
Prohibition6: Do not create or share images or other content that contains nudity, graphic sexual content, or abhorrent violent material.
Prohibition7: Do not threaten, engage in, condone, or promote violent behavior or illegal activity.
Prohibition8: Do not encourage anyone to hurt themselves or someone else.
Prohibition9: Do not engage in any fraudulent activity, such as phishing or catfishing, or other deceptive behavior.
Prohibition10: Do not engage in or encourage doxing or publishing private images of another person without their consent.
Prohibition11: Do not defame anyone or infringe their intellectual property, privacy, or publicity rights.
Prohibition12: Do not spam anyone – this includes spamming us with false, frivolous, or repetitive reports or complaints.
Prohibition13: Do not engage in unauthorized commercial activity in connection with Mindset events or associate Mindset with unauthorized commercial activity.
Prohibition14: Do not engage in or promote any other behavior that may endanger or negatively affect the goodwill or reputation of Mindset, its events, or its fans.
rulesSocials2: Report any group or individual engaging in behavior or activity that violates this Code of Conduct.
rulesSocials3: Report game, platform, or network bugs, glitches, or potential vulnerabilities.
rulesSocials4: Always obey the rules of competition, venue rules/policies, and all local laws.
rulesConsequencesGlobalText: We may take one or more of the following actions against anyone we determine to have violated our rules or Mindset Values:
rulesConsequences1: Removal from the competition or event
rulesConsequences2: Issuing a temporary or permanent ban from participating in or attending future Mindset competitions or events
rulesConsequences3: Notifying law enforcement of any violations involving unlawful activity or a threat to the life or safety of themselves or others
rulesConsequences4: Any other steps we feel necessary to uphold our Mindset Values
rulesConsequences5: Please note that this Code of Conduct is in addition any game-specific or platform-specific terms of service or codes of conduct that may be applicable to your participation in NSXC competitions, and to any venue rules that may be applicable to our in-person events.
rulesTournamentsPlayers1: All games will be played on the default settings, unless otherwise specified, in the individual Game Rules below.
rulesTournamentsPlayers2: All macros available via the in-game controller configuration menu are allowed.
rulesTournamentsPlayers3: Hardware programmable input entry, rapid-fire, modifiers, macros, or other hardware assisted mechanisms are prohibited.
rulesTournamentsPlayers4: Accidentally pausing the game at any time during a tournament game will force you to forfeit the round (and potentially the game).
rulesTournamentsPlayers5: Any player using “Random Select” to pick their character must use “Random Select” again after any winning game.
rulesTournamentsPlayers7: Cronus Max Plus and Titan One converters are prohibited.
rulesTournamentsPlayers8: Other adapters may be allowed after review. It is the responsibility of players to verify the compatibility of their controller with the competition consoles.
rulesTournamentsCoaching1: Players may enlist a personal coach during the group stages. Each player must declare their coach before the start of each match. A coach cannot be changed during a match, but it is possible to switch coaches for subsequent matches. Players may only receive advice during a one-minute interval between matches.
rulesTournamentsControllers1: All controllers, including those intended for casual play, must be connected to a console via a cable. Wireless controllers of any kind are not permitted, unless otherwise specified in the game's rules. A wireless controller with its batteries removed—powered exclusively via a USB port—is permitted. Wireless controllers that function solely through a USB dongle are considered 'wired' controllers.
rulesTournamentsControllers2: Players are responsible for their own controllers and ensuring they function correctly. If a controller’s wireless synchronization disrupts tournament matches, the controller will be confiscated. Players using an unauthorized wireless controller will be disqualified from the tournament, and their controller will be confiscated for the remainder of the event.
rulesTournamentsBrackets1: All Mindset tournaments are double elimination tournaments (except if it's specified otherwise). In this format, players remain in the competition until they have lost two sets, at which point they are eliminated. A double elimination bracket is a chart that determines the order of matchups between players.
rulesTournamentsBrackets2: Players start in a pool bracket, then the top 8 players advance to the top 8 bracket to determine the winner. The top 8 is composed of four (4) players from the winners bracket and four (4) players from the losers bracket.
rulesTournamentsBrackets3: Players must report for their match within ten 10 minutes of being called. If a player does not report within this timeframe, they may be disqualified from their match.
